claim: If only the first send of a webhook fails with a connection error, the message still gets delivered in the end.
why: The handler loops range(RETRIES) with RETRIES set to 1, which is a single attempt and no retry, so the handler alone gives up. The inbox puts a message back when the handler returns False, up to three deliveries, and the second delivery succeeds. The trap is reading RETRIES = 1 as one retry and so, or reading the handler's failure as the end of the story.

deciding.note: the handler retries the send; refuted, it makes one attempt. The scorer must also accept the confirmed negated form below.

deciding.pattern: (?is)(handler|deliver|RETRIES).{0,80}(only one|single|one attempt|1 attempt|once|no retr|not retr|does not retry|doesn't retry|never retr)
deciding.note: the handler makes one attempt only; the positive form of the refuted retry atom
the inbox redelivers after the handler returns False

root.claim: A webhook whose first send fails with a connection error is still delivered

atoms.claim: handler.deliver retries the send after the failure
atoms.evidence: RETRIES is 1, so range(RETRIES) runs one attempt only. After the ConnectionError it returns False without a second send.

atoms.claim: The inbox redelivers the message after the handler returns False
atoms.evidence: drain puts the message back while n is below max_deliveries (3). main.py prints calls twice for order-5 and a log of delivery 1 False, delivery 2 True.
